lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding

nextStoryContext: Fixed the reviewer-flagged product-name self-contradiction in docs/positioning.md: sections 1-3 (category definition, unique-position thesis, competitive landscape) previously called the product 'cam' in 13 bare-word-boundary spots (lines 3, 7x2, 15, 23, 33, 37, 47x3, 57, 60, 65, 69), directly contradicting section 4.5's demotion of `cam` to an undocumented legacy symlink and ADR 0049's explicit line-28 mandate that 'this ADR, docs/positioning.md, and any prose referencing the product name use Garboard' this cycle. Root-cause fix chosen (of the two the finding offered): renamed every product-name occurrence in sections 1-3 to Garboard (grammar-adjusted: cam's -> Garboard's, cam is -> Garboard is, cam does -> Garboard does, than cam -> than Garboard, closest to cam -> closest to Garboard), leaving section 4's two remaining bare-'cam' occurrences (line 89's historical 'moving away from the cam name', line 122's ADR-quoting 'cam, the name this product ran under ... is demoted to an undocumented legacy symlink') untouched, since those are deliberate references to the legacy name inside the naming-decision narrative itself, not the product identity being asserted. This makes ADR 0049 line 40's claim ('docs/positioning.md ... are written against Garboard as the settled product name') actually true. Confirmed via grep '\bcam\b' before/after: 15 occurrences reduced to 2 (both in section 4, both intentional). Swept for em-dash and emoji regressions on the full file post-edit (both clean). No tests reference docs/positioning.md content, so no test changes were needed. Full check:all spine (typecheck, tests 5585 pass/0 fail, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps) ran green; no file-size/coverage ceiling needed raising since this is a same-line-count text substitution. If further US-R1-00N review-round fix stories exist in prd.json, each targets a distinct reviewer finding; read that story's own notes field for its specific defect before touching any file.
